samples.summary: New `isStyleOnInSelection()` re-implements the range-dispatch walk that already exists twice in `editor.ts` instead of reusing/extracting it
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2773` (`getRangeStyleSummary`) and `editor.ts:1088` (`stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`, whose comment says it uses "the same block/offset dispatch `getRangeStyleSummary` uses") already contain the cell-range / cross-block / same-cell / same-block dispatch plus the per-inline overlap test. This diff adds a third ~130-line copy inside `TextEditor` (its own comment admits it "Mirrors `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s range walk"). The repo's stated expectation is reuse of shared traversal code; the walk should be extracted into a shared helper (e.g. alongside `Doc.applyInlineStyle` or a `range-runs` util) that both the EditorAPI summary and `TextEditor` call, so the three copies cannot drift.

samples.summary: Keyboard range read omits named-style inline defaults, so keyboard and toolbar can still disagree — the acceptance goal of the fix
samples.evidence: `isStyleOnInSelection` tests `(inline.style as Record<string, unknown>)[key]` only. `getRangeStyleSummary` (editor.ts:2847 / :2791) layers `styleDefaultsForBlock(block)` = `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), doc.document.styles)` under each run, and named styles can carry `bold` (see `packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts:97`: `resolveStyleInline('heading-1', docStyles)` → `{ fontSize: 28, bold: true }`). On such a block with no explicit run bold, the toolbar reports on → click removes, while Cmd+B computes off → applies bold. The todo's stated outcome ("Without it the keyboard and the fixed toolbar disagreed on the same selection") is therefore only partially met.

finding.summary: New `isStyleOnInSelection()` re-implements the range-dispatch walk that already exists twice in `editor.ts` instead of reusing/extracting it
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2773` (`getRangeStyleSummary`) and `editor.ts:1088` (`stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`, whose comment says it uses "the same block/offset dispatch `getRangeStyleSummary` uses") already contain the cell-range / cross-block / same-cell / same-block dispatch plus the per-inline overlap test. This diff adds a third ~130-line copy inside `TextEditor` (its own comment admits it "Mirrors `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s range walk"). The repo's stated expectation is reuse of shared traversal code; the walk should be extracted into a shared helper (e.g. alongside `Doc.applyInlineStyle` or a `range-runs` util) that both the EditorAPI summary and `TextEditor` call, so the three copies cannot drift.

verdict.reason: All three claimed sites exist as described. editor.ts:2773-2963 (`getRangeStyleSummary`) contains the cell-range/cross-block/same-cell/same-block dispatch plus the per-inline overlap test (2854). editor.ts:1072-1192 (`stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`) is a second copy, and its own comment at 1079-1081 admits it is "the same block/offset dispatch `getRangeStyleSummary` uses (cell-range rectangle, cross-block, same-cell multi-block, same-block)"; a further partial copy sits at text-box-editor.ts:879-916. The diff's new `isStyleOnInSelection` (text-editor.ts:3005-3122) is a third ~120-line copy of the same dispatch, with its comment at 3061 conceding it "Mirrors `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s range walk". I confirmed no shared traversal helper exists to reuse: grep for forEachRun|rangeRuns|range-runs|collectRuns|visitRange across packages/ returns only the per-file local closures, and neither Doc.applyInlineStyle (model/document.ts:349) nor store/block-helpers.ts:310 exposes a reusable range-run walk. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, it is reachable (called from toggleStyle at text-editor.ts:2894), and duplication/reuse is explicitly in this lens's lane where "duplicates an existing module" is rated major. The task doc at docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:49-54 does prescribe the walk "inside the `TextEditor` class", which mitigates, but a self-authored checklist does not make the structural duplication unreal or non-blocking under this rubric.

finding.summary: Keyboard range read omits named-style inline defaults, so keyboard and toolbar can still disagree — the acceptance goal of the fix
finding.evidence: `isStyleOnInSelection` tests `(inline.style as Record<string, unknown>)[key]` only. `getRangeStyleSummary` (editor.ts:2847 / :2791) layers `styleDefaultsForBlock(block)` = `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), doc.document.styles)` under each run, and named styles can carry `bold` (see `packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts:97`: `resolveStyleInline('heading-1', docStyles)` → `{ fontSize: 28, bold: true }`). On such a block with no explicit run bold, the toolbar reports on → click removes, while Cmd+B computes off → applies bold. The todo's stated outcome ("Without it the keyboard and the fixed toolbar disagreed on the same selection") is therefore only partially met.

verdict.reason: Verified in-tree: `isStyleOnInSelection` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3005-3025) decides add-vs-remove from `inline.style[key]` alone (line 3021), and its caret fallback `getStyleAtCursor` (text-editor.ts:2973-2987) also returns raw run style. A grep of the entire text-editor.ts for `resolveStyle|blockStyleId|named-styles|document.styles` yields no matches, so there is no indirect layering anywhere in the keyboard path. The toolbar side does layer named-style inline defaults per run: `styleDefaultsForBlock` (editor.ts:986-988) is applied in `getRangeStyleSummary` at editor.ts:2847/2855 and 2791/2796. The divergence is reachable without any user override, since built-in `heading-6` carries `italic: true` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91) and overrides may add `bold` (resolveStyleInline merge, named-styles.ts:126). Inline defaults are not baked into runs — the store materializes only block spacing (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:102-120,269) — so a heading run with no explicit italic makes the toolbar report ON (writes italic:false) while Cmd+I computes OFF (writes italic:true, a visual no-op). The agreement goal is stated in the change's own task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:29-34 "same named-style defaults" and :49-54 "Without it the keyboard and the fixed toolbar disagreed on the same selection"), and its "Out of scope" section (:65-72) does not exclude named-style defaults. Hence an acceptance goal is only partially met — major-kind under the spec-conformance lane. No counterexample exists to refute the absence.

finding.summary: Keyboard shortcut path still reproduces #715 — only the toolbar was fixed
finding.evidence: `TextEditor.toggleStyle` (invoked from Cmd/Ctrl+B / I / U / Shift+X at text-editor.ts:872-890) still decides add-vs-remove from `getStyleAtCursor()`, the exact caret sampling the issue identifies as wrong for backward selections. After this change, backward-selecting `cd` inside a bold run and pressing Cmd+B remains a permanent no-op, while clicking the toolbar B works — the same document now behaves differently through two entry points. The task file (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:52-56) declares this out of scope and says it is 'Recorded as a known limitation', but no design doc under docs/design/ records it; the limitation lives only in a task file that gets archived. If the issue's outcome is 'the Bold toggle works on backward selections', the keyboard half is unmet.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. `toggleStyle` (text-editor.ts:2888-2901) decides add-vs-remove from `this.isStyleOnInSelection(key)` — a genuine range walk over the selection's inline runs (text-editor.ts:3005-3049, incl. the tableCellRange rectangle) — and uses the `getStyleAtCursor()`-derived `visual[key]` only as a fallback via `inRange ?? !!visual[key]` when there is no selection or the range holds no text runs. The keyboard handlers for b/i/u/Shift+X (text-editor.ts:869-892) call that same `toggleStyle`, so the keyboard path is range-aware, not caret-sampled. The finding also misreads the task file: the Out-of-scope section is lines 65-72 and lists only the collapsed-caret `<=` boundary and the slim toolbar `pressed` state; lines 49-54 are a completed `[x]` task explicitly requiring the keyboard path to decide from the range via `isStyleOnInSelection()`. Regression coverage for the keyboard entry point exists (backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:107,168,178,188: 'Cmd+B on a backward, unstyled range applies bold (was a silent no-op)'). With no defect present, there is no unmet acceptance criterion and no known limitation needing a design doc.
